newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: AMG's Khumalo now formally JCI chairman.
newsitem.headline: AMG's Khumalo now formally JCI chairman.

text.p: Black empowerment consortium African Mining Group's Mzi Khumalo on Wednesday was formally appointed chairman of mining conglomerate JCI Ltd, the group said.
Khumalo will be replacing Pat Retief who is now retired.
AMG's Reuel Khoza was appointed as a JCI director.

JCI said that further directors drawn from AMG would be appointed to its board following the conclusion of the financial transaction between AMG and Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd and De Beers.
"This is an historic occasion for both our company and for our country. JCI is now the first black-controlled mining house in South African history," said managing director Bill Nairn.
AMG last year won a bid to purchase Anglo's 34.9 percent stake, or 52.8 million shares in JCI for 54.50 rand a share.
AMG will hold the investment in JCI through Saflife Ltd.
The consortium will also have a right of first refusal for five years in respect of 12.7 percent of JCI shares being retained by Anglo and De Beers.
The deal gives black business a significant stake in the South African mining industry for the first time.
